### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**9** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/index.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsService (symbol, a top-level class), SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsService (symbol, a top-level class), AnalyticsServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsService (symbol, a top-level class), JsonColumnFieldClass (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-5.mdx`  _(via SqlDriver (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-6.mdx`  _(via AnalyticsService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `121f3531c893b2387613283bee20aea0f4a4b388` — the merge of head `fe18f1094781cc748bc6fd15aa3ff417ab547030` into base `bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 121f3531c893b2387613283bee20aea0f4a4b388 && git checkout 121f3531c893b2387613283bee20aea0f4a4b388
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0 fe18f1094781cc748bc6fd15aa3ff417ab547030 && git checkout -B drift-repro bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0 && git merge --no-ff fe18f1094781cc748bc6fd15aa3ff417ab547030

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d07e6802db3af8d462238231a40c949059649114`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/json-column-comparison-refusal.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/preview-evaluator.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/types.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/dataset-single-value-media-refusal-36190.test.ts + read in the cited code, not reviewed: packages/core/src/utils/json-column-operator-refusal.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-database-helpers.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-rotation.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-schema-sync.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-top-level.ts, packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/contains-membership-sql.ts, .changeset/config.json, .changeset/36168-dataset-json-column-refusal.md (precedent on `main`)

Inputs read: card #36190 body and its five comments (triage 7069730609, claim 7096730827, progress 7103673343 and 7111288014, os-dev-report 7111805621; no ruling and no earlier record on the card), PR #36771 body and its 10-file list, the net diff `origin/main...d07e6802`, and the check-runs on the head. Check-runs: every run that was scheduled completed `success` (Build Core, Test Core 1-10/10 and its roll-up, Type Check workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Lint & Repo Gates and its seven lint families, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Test UI, Live E2E UI); the rest are path-scheduled `skipped`; none failed, none neutral. Seven Test Core shards were still running at the first read and were re-read to completion before this verdict; the head did not move.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of the dataset query door, native face (`NativeSQLStrategy.buildFilterClause`) — narrowed, right.** A leaf whose normalised operator maps to a member of `JSON_COLUMN_INCOMPATIBLE_OPERATORS` on a column whose storing driver answers `'single-value-media'` now throws `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 before anything binds. It covers the caller's `where` (the door's `runtimeFilter` merged in), the dataset's own `filter` and the measures' `filter`s, because all three reach the one call at the `[#36168]` site; the read scope does not reach it, as before. Previously 200 with a wrong count (card table). The population is strictly the old one plus this class: `comparisonColumnClass` keeps the declared-shape arm first, so no `multi-value-or-json` verdict or sentence moves.
- **Accept set of the draft preview (`lowerPreviewRowFilters`) — narrowed, right against the card.** Same class, judged once over the lowered `where` before any row is read. The card's Done-when names the preview explicitly, so the refusal of a count the preview used to compute over bare drafted ids is the card's order, not the dev's choice.
- **Unknown-dialect decline (`jsonConstructOnUnknownDialectIn`) — right.** For a comparison it now returns `whereComparisonColumnClass(...) !== undefined`; for the old population that is `isJsonStoredShape(shape)` exactly as before (the `$empty` arm was never reachable for a comparison), plus the media class, which is then handed to the ObjectQL strategy whose driver refuses. The membership and `$empty` arms below it are untouched.
- **Not narrowed — right.** `$contains` / `$notContains`, `$null` / `$exists` / `$empty`, `$eq: null` / `$ne: null`, an empty `$in` / `$nin`, every operator on a scalar column, and every operator on a media column once the deployment has moved it: `SqlDriver.jsonColumnFieldClass` answers `undefined` there (`isJsonField` reads `mediaColumnIsJson`, i.e. `!fileColumnsMoved`, at registration), and `undefined` is not judged.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/driver-sql`: `SqlDriver.jsonColumnFieldClass` `protected` → `public`, body unchanged — additive, right.** It is the same predicate `assertOperatorAppliesToColumn` asks on the data door, so the analytics faces and the data door cannot come to disagree about the population or about which side of the ADR-0104 window a deployment is on. The same member becomes public on the in-tree subclasses (`TursoDriver`, `SqliteWasmDriver`); neither overrides it.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/driver-turso`: `REMOTE_FACE_ANSWERS` gains `jsonColumnFieldClass: 'inherited'` — right.** The ledger is a `satisfies Record` keyed by `keyof SqlDriver`, so the row is owed the moment the member is public, and `inherited` is true of the code: `TursoDriver` does not redeclare the member and already hands it to the remote transport (`setJsonColumnResolver`, turso-driver.ts:2180).
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/service-analytics`: `AnalyticsServiceConfig.jsonColumnFieldClass?` and `DatasetScopedStrategyContext.jsonColumnFieldClass?` — additive and optional, right.** A host that wires nothing keeps its behaviour. `refusePreviewJsonColumnComparisons` changes its second parameter (`shapeOf` → `classOf`) and `lowerPreviewRowFilters` gains a sixth optional parameter; neither is exported from the package index, and the only caller of each is in the diff.
- **Published spec (`packages/spec`): untouched.** No schema, no authorable key, no contract type moves; the hook is declared on the package-local context for the reason `declaredFieldType` is.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — on the PR body and on the changeset body, as the card's Done-when orders; `Metadata-protocol: none` on both.

`patch` on `@objectstack/service-analytics` and `@objectstack/driver-sql` is the level the rule gives: a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition. The changeset carries the banner, a FROM → TO mapping, the "Not moved" boundary, the caller's fix, and exactly one marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`). `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: `DatasetSchema` accepts every filter it accepted before, and what moves is the answer at query time; this is the reading the precedent changeset for #36168 on `main` took for the identical change one class over. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on the head.

N1 (nit) — the changeset frontmatter names `@objectstack/driver-sql` and `@objectstack/service-analytics` only. The diff also moves `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts` (an exported const gains a key), and the visibility change lands in the published `.d.ts` of `TursoDriver` and `SqliteWasmDriver`. All four packages sit in the one `fixed` group, so no version is wrong; the effect is that those packages' `CHANGELOG.md` carries no line for it, where the house precedent (the `driver-sql` CHANGELOG entry naming `driver-sqlite-wasm` for an inherited signature change) names the subclass package. The visible body also says nothing a `driver-sql` reader can act on: the "becomes public" sentence sits inside the ADR-0087 HTML comment. A one-line addition could say that a subclass redeclaring `jsonColumnFieldClass` as `protected` must widen it. Fixable on the changeset alone.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the os-dev-report; nothing to answer.
- **File-surface breach, answered: accepted.** The claim's surface was `packages/services/service-analytics/src/**`; the diff also touches `driver-sql` (one visibility keyword and a two-line pointer) and `driver-turso` (one ledger row). The report explains it, and the card itself says why it is unavoidable: "the analytics host has no hook today for the column's storage state". The producer of that fact is the driver; a second copy of the ADR-0104 window question on the analytics side would have been the wrong design. The `driver-turso` row is forced by its own typecheck.
- **Claim line mismatch, answered: no effect.** The claim comment says `Clause-②: no`; the card, the PR body and the changeset all say `no (narrowing)`, and those are the lines the gates read.
- **Out-of-scope finding (`$contains` on a single-value media column), escalated to the seat.** The dev's inference is consistent with the code read here: `whereContainsMembershipSql` returns `null` unless the DECLARED shape is JSON-stored (contains-membership-sql.ts:125), so on this class the native face falls to text-match over the stored JSON string, while `@objectstack/core`'s own docblock records that the data door's membership test answers no rows there. Two faces, two answers, for an operator the refusal set leaves out on purpose. It is outside #36190's Done-when and this PR's changeset says so honestly ("Not moved"). It is unmeasured; the seat owes a measurement and, if it reproduces, a card (Prime Directive 10) rather than a line that lives only in a report. Not a finding on this head.
- **Deviation 1 (`check:type-check-debt` not measured locally), answered: covered.** `Type Check · debt ledger` is `success` on the head.
- **Deviations 2 and 3 (first runs at an earlier head; `main` moved after the merge), answered: accepted.** The check-runs on `d07e6802` are the gate verdicts; the ablation at `34268214` is evidence about a function that did not change afterwards and is not relied on for this verdict.
- **Facade line ceiling, answered: accepted.** `sql-driver.ts` lands exactly on its registered ceiling with the rationale on the analytics-side docblock; the repo gates are green, and no ceiling was raised.
- **PR body's ask of the maintainer** (whether "an attachment field cannot be filtered by value, only by presence" may go out as stated): not a new position. It is the sentence `@objectstack/core` already publishes for this class on the data door; this PR adds no wording of its own. No ruling is owed for it.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): clean.** No id materialisation and no in-app join is added. The refusal runs before compile, and the storage fact is one registry read on the driver, per judged leaf. Nothing that SQL could answer is moved into memory; the preview face evaluates drafted rows in memory as it already did.

### ④ Design judgment

The question is whether this narrowing takes a declared capability away at the consumer, or makes the spec's own refusal real. It is the second.

- **The refusal is already the published contract.** `JSON_COLUMN_INCOMPATIBLE_OPERATORS`, the `JsonColumnFieldClass` pair and the `'single-value-media'` sentence are on `main` in `@objectstack/core` (#21236), and `driver-sql`'s `where` and the dataset door's ObjectQL strategy already give it. Nothing on `main` declares that `=` / `$in` / `$ne` answer on a single-value media column inside the ADR-0104 window; the card measured the opposite, 200 with a count of 0 or of every row. A wrong count is not a capability, so nothing declared is narrowed at the consumer.
- **The capability that IS declared stays delivered.** A media column that has been moved holds the bare id, comparisons on it are meant to answer, and they do: the class is asked of the driver, whose answer is `undefined` after the move. The consumer does not re-derive the window; had it read the declared type (`image`) instead, it would have refused a moved deployment and taken the capability away. That is the design choice that makes this a refusal made real rather than a consumer-side narrowing.
- **One predicate, three doors.** The analytics faces call the method the data door calls, on the driver `getDriverForObject` returns for the leaf's own object, so a joined dimension is judged by the driver that stores it. Wording comes from the one core builder with the class passed in, so the media class is told about the column move and never about `$contains`.
- **Attempts to break it.** (a) Over-refusal through the driver's other class: the plugin passes `'multi-value-or-json'` through, but `comparisonColumnClass` acts on the stored answer only when it is `'single-value-media'`, so a driver answer cannot widen #36168's population; the two populations differ only by the driver-internal aliases `object` / `array`, which no author can declare. (b) A host with no SQL driver (memory, mongo), no data engine, or a hook that throws: `undefined` at four separate guards, not judged, behaviour unchanged. (c) Operator spellings: the native face maps the normalised leaf back through `CUBE_TO_MONGO_OP` to the same set; the preview applies the same null-comparand and empty-list exemptions the native leaf has. (d) Refusing everything: the test's scalar control and `$null` control answer with exact counts on all three faces. (e) Turso remote: the ledger row is true, and refusing there matches the remote transport's own refusal. None of these broke.
- **Tests against the contract.** 14 tests on the production composition (real plugin, engine and `SqlDriver` on SQLite), `image` and `file`, four spellings, three faces, code and status and field and class-specific words, plus the dataset's own `filter` and three controls. This meets the card's "pins on `image` and `file` with a scalar control".

N2 (nit) — the moved-deployment arm ("Not moved … a deployment whose media columns have moved") is stated in the changeset and holds by reading, but no test in this suite drives the dataset door over a driver with `fileColumnsMoved: true`. It is the one cell where a later edit could turn the refusal into a taken-away capability without a red test on this face. A follow-up pin, not a change to this head.

N3 (nit) — stale prose in `json-column-comparison-refusal.ts`: the docblock of `refuseWhereJsonColumnComparison` still reads "is declared multi-valued or JSON-stored", and the module header's "prescribes `$contains`" bullet is now true of one class only (the `[#36190]` bullet below it corrects it). `whereComparisonColumnClass` also tests `isJsonStoredShape(shape)` and then calls `comparisonColumnClass`, which tests it again; and `preview-evaluator.ts` imports from the refusal module on two lines. No effect on behaviour.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-36190-analytics-single-media-json-refusal`
Reviewed-by: `L2 reviewer (isolated sub-agent of session_011y7As6YDLR8TJVDpdXzJyV)`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

- 结论:退回修改(REWORK),只改文字面，代码不动。修复本身对：数据集查询和草稿预览对单值附件列(仍以 JSON 存)的 `=` / `$in` / `$ne` 现在会和数据接口一样直接拒绝(400),不再返回错的计数。
- 要补的只是声明:这次同时公开了一个驱动方法和一个分析服务配置项，按规则要写 `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`,并给 driver-turso 补 changeset。无需你做任何事。

## 席位核对 — REWORK · head d07e6802db3af8d462238231a40c949059649114 · card #36190

L2 record at this head: comment 7112462731 (PASS, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, narrowing face; no must-fix, no should-fix, nits N1–N3) · 2026-11-23T20:05Z. I read it against GitHub (`git diff origin/main...d07e6802`, `l1-face.mjs --pr 36771`, `pr-state.mjs`, report 7111805621), not against the report alone.

### Checklist
- Shape: open, draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #36190`. No closing keyword binds another card.
- Code: `comparisonColumnClass` takes the declared JSON shape first (`multi-value-or-json`, as before #36190), then the storing driver's `single-value-media`, and otherwise leaves the column unjudged. The plugin reads the driver through `getDriverForObject`, answers `undefined` on every tier that cannot answer, and passes only the two known classes on. The preview wraps the call in `try`. No SQL push-down finding.
- Title `fix(analytics)!:` and changeset headline with `!`; BREAKING banner with FROM / TO / Not moved / the fix; one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker; `Skills-docs:` line present and true; level `patch` under `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- Dogfood battery in full at this head (report 7111805621): `d07e6802` · VERDICT command-exit 0 · 487 files passed, 3 skipped · 4125 tests passed, 68 skipped · no failures.
- Gates at this head: 37 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending (Test Core 1–10/10 included). Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are success, and `mergeable_state` is clean.

### REWORK items (prose only)
1. **`Clause-②` must read `yes (narrowing)`.** `Clause-②` asks whether the diff widens or narrows a published accept set or public surface (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, the level-axis note). This diff widens two published surfaces besides the narrowing: `SqlDriver.jsonColumnFieldClass` goes from `protected` to `public` on the class `@objectstack/driver-sql` exports (and so on `TursoDriver` and `SqliteWasmDriver`, which extend it), and the exported `AnalyticsServiceConfig` (`@objectstack/service-analytics` root) gains the optional key `jsonColumnFieldClass`. The same move on main is declared `yes (narrowing)`: `.changeset/35525-analytics-disabled-package.md`, where `AnalyticsServiceConfig` gained the optional `isObjectPackageDisabled` beside a door refusal. Fix in the PR body and the changeset: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — widened: …; narrowed: …`, naming both surfaces. Take the "only becomes public" sentence out of the ADR-0087 HTML comment so the release text says it (L2 N1). The marker category and level `patch` stay. The L2 graded `no (narrowing)` as right. I rule against it on the clause's written meaning and the #35525 precedent. The tier is the same either way.
2. **Changeset entry for `@objectstack/driver-turso` (l1-face flag, L2 N1).** It is published, `src/turso-driver.ts` moves, and its `TursoDriver` `.d.ts` gains the public member. Add `'@objectstack/driver-turso': patch`. `@objectstack/driver-sqlite-wasm` is not touched by the diff, but its published `.d.ts` gains the member too. An entry there is optional.

### Owed after the fix
- A same-head contract review delta at the new head, by the same reviewer, because the handoff reads a same-head record. No dogfood rerun is needed if only `.changeset/` and the PR body move.

### Accepted deviations
- `check:type-check-debt` was NOT MEASURED locally. It is covered by CI `Type Check · debt ledger` success at this head.
- L2 N2 (no dataset-door pin over a driver with moved media columns) and N3 (stale prose in `json-column-comparison-refusal.ts`, a redundant re-check, a split import): accepted. N2 belongs on a follow-up pin.

### Out of scope, disposition
- The dev's `$contains` note: on a single-value media column inside the ADR-0104 window, the native face text-matches the stored JSON string, while the data door's JSON membership finds no row. The L2 read is consistent with it: `whereContainsMembershipSql` reads only the declared shape. It is a cross-face disagreement at a named location, so it clears filing-gate ① once it has a `reach:`. One measured reading through `POST /api/v1/analytics/dataset/query` beside `POST /api/v1/data/:object/query` on the #36190 fixture is enough. Without the reading it is a p3 for a sweep card.
